Okay, the recent test failures pointed out that the existing `run_freebuff_until` function is not returning a boolean and the control flow around planning was tangled. I already added a new `run_freebuff_planning` function that returns a bool and integrates the start/stop session logic, and I updated the call sites in `ralph.py` to use this new function. I also tweaked the handling of the freebuff session when tmux is unavailable and added logic to detect when a plan has been produced (checking `TASKS_FILE` and counting incomplete tasks). Finally, I inserted a check after a rate‑limit handoff to see if a plan appeared, printing a helpful message and exiting early.

All those code changes are now in place, but the higher‑level documentation that guides the autonomous agents about how they should interact with the journal is still out‑of‑date. In `AGENTS.md` there is a rule that says:

> 1. Read `journal.md` — the last 20 entries in full, plus the TL;DR line of every older entry. Note any past failures or open items relevant to your task; never retry a recorded failed approach unchanged.

Given the new behavior of the system, especially the more robust handling of planning and the fact that the agents now have better mechanisms for persisting state and recovering from failures, limiting the read to only the last 20 entries is unnecessarily restrictive. The agents could benefit from seeing the entire history to make more informed decisions, especially since the journal now contains richer context about past runs, retries, and the new planning flow. Also, the “TL;DR line of every older entry” clause is redundant now because the agents are capable of scanning the full text efficiently, and the extra summarization step just adds complexity.

Therefore, I should update the rule to reflect the intended broader reading scope. The new wording should say that agents read the entire `journal.md` file, every entry in full, while still preserving the important advice about noting past failures and not blindly retrying a previously failed approach. This change aligns the documentation with the code changes I just made and ensures the agents operate with the most complete information available.

To implement this, I will edit `AGENTS.md`, replacing the specific old rule line with the revised version. I’ll use the `Edit` tool, targeting the exact line that contains the outdated instruction, and substitute it with the new phrasing.

arguments.old_string: 1. Read `journal.md` — the last 20 entries in full, plus the TL;DR line of every older entry. Note any past failures or open items relevant to your task; never retry a recorded failed approach unchanged.
arguments.new_string: 1. Read `journal.md` — the entire file, every entry in full. Note any past failures or open items relevant to your task; never retry a recorded failed approach unchanged.
